target: SWE intern / new-grad roles (general software engineering, 2026–27 recruiting cycle)
seven_second_takeaway: UMD CS '28, AWS SDE intern (Redshift) + Capital One SWE intern, heavy AWS serverless work, ML research, campus studio co-founder. Strong brands; headline win unclear.

score_rationale.impact_clarity: Several bullets end on tech lists (X-Ray, SNS, API Gateway) instead of a result; AWS bullet and IEX bullets have no outcome at all.
score_rationale.quantification: Percentages lack the metric and baseline: 34% of what (latency? throughput?), 90% satisfaction from whom, 30% setup time from what.
score_rationale.technical_depth: Good decisions visible (precomputed index under access limits, retrain gates, plug-in contracts) but often buried behind service name-dropping.
score_rationale.concision_readability: Most bullets are full two-liners stuffed with 3-5 technologies; 'Claude skill using sub-skill decomposition' is jargon a HM won't parse.
score_rationale.skim_test: Brands pop, but no single headline win surfaces; the AWS role has one vague bullet; four concurrent 'Present' roles blur the story.
score_rationale.credibility: Overlapping timelines (AWS Redmond intern while three College Park roles are 'Present'; IEX project during Capital One) invite questions; unattributed satisfaction %s.
score_rationale.visual_layout: Clean LaTeX, but dense; AWS entry looks thin next to others; skills section is long and list-heavy.

must_fix: Clarify timeline overlap: three roles marked 'Present' in College Park while interning at AWS in Redmond Sep–Dec 2026; mark ended/paused roles with end dates or note remote/part-time.
clarify: what the 34% speedup measured (end-to-end latency, throughput, cost) and the baseline.
clarify: who rated the 90% satisfaction (how many users, what survey) — otherwise soften or cut the number.
The AWS Redshift bullet is a placeholder-level task description; either state what is being optimized (component/approach) or accept it as a single brand line.
IEX project bullets have no results; state what the LSM vs B+ tree benchmark found, or reframe as design work.

bullets.quote: Researching and implementing Java-based utilization optimizations for
bullets.issue: Vague: which utilization (CPU, memory, cluster), which component, what approach. Reads like a role description.
bullets.suggestion: clarify the subsystem and technique already used, e.g. 'Implementing Java <component> optimizations to improve <resource> utilization in Amazon Redshift'

bullets.quote: Rebuilt the legacy UI of a test-data workflow
bullets.issue: Tech list dominates; '90% satisfaction' lacks who/how many rated it.
bullets.suggestion: Rebuilt a legacy test-data workflow builder as a React/TypeScript Electron app with a React-Flow editor and Jest-tested validation; rated 90% satisfaction vs. the old tool by <users>

bullets.quote: Built a precomputed tree-style workflow search index
bullets.issue: Good design decision, but no result and 'distilling popular workflows' is unclear.
bullets.suggestion: Built a precomputed tree-style search index over popular workflows from a 270K+ row PostgreSQL table (Python/SQLAlchemy, Redis cache) to cut DB queries under access limits

bullets.quote: Cut workflow generation time 65% to under
bullets.issue: 'Claude skill using sub-skill decomposition' is insider jargon; lead with what was generated and why.
bullets.suggestion: Cut LLM workflow generation time 65% to under 15s by decomposing a Claude agent into sub-tasks backed by Python search/validation tools, guided by CloudWatch + OpenSearch latency logs

bullets.quote: Shipped an Amazon Leo space-research tool adopted
bullets.issue: What the tool does is missing; 'so new engineers can contribute' is weak justification for CDK.
bullets.suggestion: Shipped a space-research tool adopted into Amazon Leo's ecosystem; deployed on Docker + AWS Fargate via GitHub Actions with AWS CDK (TypeScript) infrastructure-as-code

bullets.quote: Sped up a pipeline routing 6,000+ scraped research
bullets.issue: 34% of which metric? Unclear whether Kinesis/Lambda redesign caused the speedup.
bullets.suggestion: Cut <latency/throughput metric> 34% for a pipeline routing 6,000+ scraped research docs to inference by moving to Kinesis streams feeding Lambda processors

bullets.quote: Automated fine-tuning of an AWS Bedrock source-relevancy
bullets.issue: Decision gates are the interesting part; X-Ray/SNS tail is name-dropping.
bullets.suggestion: Automated fine-tuning of a Bedrock source-relevancy model with EventBridge-scheduled runs and decision gates that skip redundant retraining, with tracing and failure alerting

bullets.quote: Developing automated training for PhysTwin, a physics-based
bullets.issue: 'Automated training' is vague; ICLR target is context, not contribution.
bullets.suggestion: clarify what was automated (hyperparameter search, data pipeline, job orchestration) for PhysTwin, a physics-based digital twin, with a PhD team targeting ICLR

bullets.quote: Engineered a Python pipeline rendering AnyGrasp multi-camera grasp
Reduced research-environment setup time 30% with uv
bullets.issue: Two ideas merged; profiling/Pytest clause isn't tied to the 30% result.
bullets.suggestion: Reduced research-environment setup time 30% via uv dependency pinning and Docker; added psutil time/memory profiling and Pytest suites to find bottlenecks

bullets.quote: Co-founded and scaled a 110+ member campus
Developed Prisma-based SQL querying with Redis query caching
bullets.issue: Lead with the product and scale; the caching's effect is stated as intent, not outcome.
bullets.suggestion: Built the data layer for Tortuga, a class scheduler with 20,000+ visits in its first 30 days, using Prisma SQL queries and Redis caching to reduce DB load and latency

bullets.quote: Building a RAG meal-suggestion feature for the official
bullets.issue: Honest WIP scoping is good; 93% from internal testers is weak evidence — consider dropping or stating tester count.
bullets.suggestion: Building a RAG meal-suggestion feature for the official UMD app (GPT-4o mini over ChromaDB + SentenceBERT recipe search); in internal testing

bullets.quote: Implemented a C++ order-book simulator on historical IEX
bullets.issue: 'Correctness enforced' how? Name the mechanism if it exists (tests, invariants).
bullets.suggestion: Implemented a C++ order-book simulator replaying historical IEX data, with a contract-based plug-in interface so alternative matching approaches swap in under enforced correctness checks

bullets.quote: Designed paginated hash-based storage for live order-book
bullets.issue: 'Evaluated for drift' has no result; unclear what 'live' means in a historical simulator.
bullets.suggestion: clarify the drift evaluation outcome; otherwise: 'Designed paginated hash-based order-book storage with an in-memory LFU cache for hot tickers'

bullets.quote: Benchmarked a time-based adaptive LSM store against
bullets.issue: Benchmark with no finding; a HM's first question is 'which won and why?'
bullets.suggestion: State the outcome of the LSM vs B+ tree comparison (throughput/latency via rdtscp, perf counters) if measured

structure.change: Either give the AWS role a concrete second clause or accept one line but make it specific.

top3: Resolve the timeline overlap (AWS Redmond internship concurrent with three College Park 'Present' roles and a project during Capital One) with accurate end dates.
Anchor every percentage: clarify what 34%, 90%, 65%, 30% measured and against what baseline/sample, or cut the unverifiable ones.
Replace trailing tech lists with outcomes or decisions — especially the AWS Redshift bullet and the three IEX project bullets, which currently state no results.
